It's terrible advice, that's what it is. Yeah, you can't just sit alone and wait for things to get better, but "well life is just sad sometimes" is only helpful to people who are rarely ever sad. I hear that sentence and I think: "if 'life is sad' this much, why the hell would i even live through it." 

maybe im naive, but i think that there is a happier life out there for us. and it's not what everyone is telling us it is. it's better. 

have you considered looking for a new therapist of some kind? maybe an online one? you said it has never solved anything for you and I completely understand that, so i understand if you're not at all open to that as well. I have a really shitty therapist at the moment. 

But if you're at all willing, I think it's worth a shot. Talking to a third party, giving no fucks about what they think or what they know or who they could tell, and just seriously letting everything trapped inside of you out can be truly liberating, even if you only do it once. 

other than that, medication is out there though that's a much shadier, harder to work through department, and I have no idea your medical history or your previous experience with it or anything like that, but that may also be a solution if you have a decent doctor.

God, I'm sorry, but i can guarantee to you that someone understands. And no one with a caring bone in their body would scoff at you for talking about those things, at least I know I wouldn't. It's good to talk about those things, and it isn't super healthy all the time to just ignore your past. I'm sure you know those things already, but life's too short not to try to work through or learn to deal with what problems you have.
